data.summary: Reports and commentary in the set described a roughly $6.34B Binance theft as a months-long operation involving malicious software, fake recruiting, an internal AI tool and misuse of wallet-signing access; Binance said about $2.85B was frozen or intercepted, and the FBI attributed the theft to North Korea-linked hackers. Commentary framed the failure as exchange custody/signing infrastructure rather than a Bitcoin protocol hack.

Builders debated prompt injection as an authorization/security bug for AI agents rather than just a chatbot quirk. Cited concerns included agents reading web pages, email, Slack or package docs and treating untrusted text as orders; suggested controls included read-only tokens, command allowlists, sandboxing and human approval before merges, deploys or payments.

Projects marketed wallet-level guardrails for agent payments: Assay described a provider allow-list and fail-closed payments to stop prompt injection from sending funds elsewhere; Grid was highlighted for MAX_USD_PER_CALL and MAX_USD_PER_BOUNTY caps; RunOva described spending ceilings with approvals above the limit using NEAR scoped keys.
Commentators quoted Yat Siu saying AI agents overspend and also “overtalk,” with a stabledash clip and follow-up framing gossipy agents and over-sharing as behavior risks that need limits.

Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon launch drew attention for claimed security and agentic performance: tweets said Google or early testers reported a 0% prompt-injection success rate on Gray Swan’s benchmark, strong CursorBench and cyber results, and availability to paid API and Ultra users.

Sui/Mysten Labs discussions centered on treating autonomous agents as untrusted by default, with proposals such as Agent Pass bounded authority, Rooms enforcing business rules, and Google Cloud/Walrus-backed verifiable logs (VAA) for agent accountability.

Security researchers warned about persistent prompt injection through agent supply chains: a Miasma/testmetest campaign reportedly poisoned GitHub repos with CLAUDE.md instructions telling coding agents to run an obfuscated setup.js without review, while a Snyk scan of 20,000 agent skills reportedly found widespread unsafe patterns and at least one skill appending remote text to global Claude instructions.

Prompt-injection incidents were cited as evidence that agentic finance needs trust and security layers: tweets referenced a Morse-code prompt injection and cases where agents were persuaded into paying out funds, arguing wallet restrictions and spending limits matter.

Users posted what they described as a leaked Claude web-app system prompt for Fable/Mythos 5.2, highlighting instructions that external pages, emails, files and tool outputs are data not orders, plus rules around memory privacy and forged notices.

Macro roundups attributed a crypto drawdown to hawkish Fed repricing after a strong payrolls print, heavy spot-Bitcoin ETF outflows, leveraged liquidations and a broader risk-off move; Bitcoin and major altcoins fell, while policy items included CFTC clearing single-stock perpetual futures and Samsung wallet supporting USDC.
